analysis.title: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
key_insights: Core PCE was 3.0% y/y in August, 0.7pp above GS's 2.3% start-of-the-year forecast for August. GS decomposes the surprise by category and driver to test whether it reflects one-offs or broader stickiness.
Computer software and accessories plus other electronics account for more than 0.3pp of the overshoot, reflecting a larger-than-expected AI-related boost to consumer prices.

Part of the electronics surprise is likely mismeasurement. Computer software and accessories still contributes 0.2pp after recent methodological changes. GS estimates the consumer electronics contribution is overstated by 0.1pp.

The software and accessories weight is roughly 30 times its CPI weight because PCE source data overstates software sales to retail customers. The PCE component has diverged significantly from its CPI analogue.
The component is not quality-adjusted like other technology components, so new AI features were likely captured as price increases rather than quantity increases.
GS expects the software and accessories contribution to ease in 2027 as memory price pressures fade.

Air transportation accounts for 0.2pp of the surprise, largely from higher jet fuel prices tied to the war with Iran. Energy cost passthrough to air transportation and other components accounts for 0.3pp in total.
Other core goods contributed 0.1pp, roughly a third of it from greater-than-expected tariff passthrough. GS raised its peak consumer tariff passthrough estimate to 80% from 70% in January.

The higher passthrough is largely offset by the decline in the effective tariff rate after the Supreme Court ruling on the IEEPA tariffs. Tariffs therefore explain only 0.1pp of the surprise across core goods.
Shelter added roughly 0.1pp to the upside surprise because it slowed by less than expected. GS still expects further shelter disinflation in coming months.
Pharmaceuticals and used vehicles subtracted a combined 0.2pp versus forecast. GS sees both as durable price-level changes unlikely to reverse.

Pharma prices fell on Medicare drug price negotiation, the TrumpRx discount program and patent expirations on several blockbuster drugs. Used vehicles are softening as H2 2025 increases unwind, with demand cooling on higher interest rates.

The oil shock, tariffs and the software and accessories component account for roughly three-fourths of the surprise and should ease over the next year. About 0.2pp of genuine upside remains, mostly from housing and other AI-exposed electronics.
GS sees no strong evidence of a significant acceleration in underlying inflation versus its start-of-year forecast and still expects core PCE to fall to 2.2% by December 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: 0.7pp above GS's 2.3% start-of-year forecast for August. GS attributes about three-fourths of the overshoot to temporary factors or mismeasurement.
GS bottom-up model projects a modest decline from August's 3.0%.
Gradual disinflation as oil, tariff, memory-price and mismeasurement effects fade.
Raised from 70% assumed in January, but largely offset by the lower effective tariff rate after the IEEPA ruling.

risk_factors: Underlying stickiness: if the overshoot is not one-off, inflation could stay higher for longer.
Shelter disinflation has been slower than GS assumed.
AI-related demand continues to push up prices in exposed electronics components.
Memory price shock fades more slowly than expected, which would prolong the software and accessories contribution.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots contributions to the August y/y core PCE surprise by component, split into oil-driven, tariff-driven and residual. Software and accessories and air transport are the largest positive contributors, and pharma & medical and used vehicles are negative.
Exhibit 5 gives GS's bottom-up core PCE model: core PCE 3.0% y/y in August 2026, 2.9% in December 2026 and 2.2% in December 2027.
geopolitical: War with Iran has raised jet fuel prices and feeds energy cost passthrough into air transportation and other core PCE components.
Supreme Court ruling on the IEEPA tariffs lowered the effective tariff rate.

tension_points.bull_case: Roughly three-fourths of the overshoot comes from the oil shock, tariffs and software and accessories mismeasurement and memory prices, all expected to fade. Core PCE falls to 2.2% by December 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: The overshoot could reflect broader underlying stickiness. About 0.2pp of genuine upside remains from housing and AI-exposed electronics, and shelter disinflation is slower than assumed.

theme_stances.key_argument: About three-fourths of the core PCE surprise comes from mismeasurement or one-time factors that should fade, so the underlying trend has not accelerated.
theme_stances.evidence: we do not see strong evidence of a significant acceleration in the underlying trend of inflation
